Read first: the two monthly headline profits are historical fits. The corresponding earlier-selected monthly accounts lost 1,371.92 and 7,049.34. All figures below retain that distinction.

What the results say

Forecast accuracy improves only slightly over copying today’s close. The saved trading profits depend on the chosen rules, timing, sizing and costs. The newer systems’ monthly historical-fit profits reverse to losses under earlier-selected rules.

Forecasting

The best model, the FT-Transformer, lowers test error by just 0.16% compared with copying today's close. A stacked model that combines three of them does 1.08% worse. High R² (0.9935) is not a sign of skill here, since the copy-today forecast scores the same.

Trading

The annual and short engines use 10 bps per side. Advanced execution adds volume-dependent impact to a 5 bps commission and 5 bps base slippage, with minimum fees and short borrowing. The long-horizon system gains 42.63% but trails holding the stock; earlier-selected monthly rules lose 1.37% and 7.05% in the two newer systems.

Short-horizon results by window

Each window is its own account that starts at 100,000 and ends flat. Windows overlap, so their profits must not be added together.

Return in each window

Solid bars use rules fitted to these final sessions. Hatched bars use rules chosen from earlier data. The dashed tick is buy-and-hold.

Compare selection methods, not just bar height.

Solid historical-fit outcomes were selected after inspecting the final windows. Earlier-selected rules use the same execution engines but different parameters. The negative earlier-selected monthly bars show that the profitable fitted rule is sensitive to the selection period.

How to read this. The solid bars were selected using the same 5, 22 and 44 sessions they are measured on, so they describe the past and say little about the future. The hatched bars are the fairer test, and they are mostly negative.

Account value

Timing of profit matters.

A flat line generally means cash or no net daily change; a jump locates the sessions that generated the outcome. Compare the four accounts within the selected window. Changing the window restarts every account, so paths are not portions of one continuous portfolio.

Weekly interpretation

The short and advanced historical fits earn 1,009.81 and 2,120.50 from one completed trade each. Both trail the 3.36% buy-and-hold return. One winning trade is a description of this week, not a stable estimate of performance.

Monthly interpretation

The advanced historical fit earns 8,076.11 from four shorts; the short strategy earns 2,541.14 from three intraday positions. Both outperform the 0.70% benchmark in this selected window. Their earlier-selected rules lose money, so selection method changes the conclusion.

Two-month interpretation

The short historical fit earns 6,052.88 and the advanced fit earns 1,961.40. The advanced system’s larger monthly profit does not carry over to the longer window. Each window restarts its cash and position state; a longer-window result is not a sum of shorter runs.

Matches the NYSE calendar

From raw prices to a forecast target

Everything is built from information available at the close of day t, to predict the close of the next trading day.

Cleaning and cross-checks

  • Yahoo and Google prices share 7,271 dates; Google has 2 dates Yahoo lacks and Yahoo has 3 that Google lacks. Yahoo was used.
  • No duplicate dates, no invalid high/low/open/close combinations, no zero or negative volume.
  • 38 days with an unchanged close, kept because repeated closes are legitimate.
  • The calendar has 1,564 weekend days, 139 regular holidays, 4 one-off closures (such as Hurricane Sandy in October 2012) and 33 early closes. No session is missing and none is extra.
  • Adjusted close is not used as a feature, because later dividend adjustments would leak into past rows.

The 31 engineered features

How TSM behaves

Returns have fat tails

Excess kurtosis is 3.97 and skew is 0.19, so large moves happen more often than a normal curve predicts. 220 days were flagged as unusual by at least one outlier test; they were inspected, not removed.

BestWorst
Day+12.65% (27 Jul 2020)−14.03% (16 Mar 2020)
Week+18.17% (7–13 Nov 2022)−14.74% (16–22 Mar 2020)
Month+38.96% (Jul 2020)−17.74% (Sep 2022)
Year+89.89% (2024)−38.08% (2022)

Prices drift, returns do not

Tests on log price cannot reject a unit root at any frequency, so price is non-stationary and needs differencing. Returns pass at every frequency.

SeriesADF pKPSS pReading
Daily log price0.6790.010not stationary
Daily return<0.0010.100stationary
Weekly log price0.6220.010not stationary
Monthly log price0.6550.043not stationary
Weekly and monthly returns<0.0010.100stationary

No weekday, month or other calendar pattern stayed significant once the many comparisons were corrected for (Benjamini–Hochberg). On the training data alone, one difference was enough: the first difference of price has an ADF p-value of 6×10⁻¹⁶, and differencing again at lag 5 brought it lower still (3×10⁻³⁰).

How the data is split

Train · 2,604
Validate · 558
Test · 559
Forecast made 18 Nov 2011 to 25 Mar 2022
28 Mar 2022 to 14 Jun 2024
17 Jun 2024 to 9 Sep 2026

Each row is one forecast made after a close (the origin) for the next close (the target). That gives 3,721 usable rows out of 3,771. The other 50 are the warm-up of the rolling features (the first 49 days) and the final day, which has no target yet. Rows stay in time order, and every scaler is fitted only on earlier data.

Test period: TSM closing price

The price rose from about $180 to $428 across the 559 test sessions, which is why holding the stock is a hard benchmark to beat.

A rising price level makes level forecasts look accurate.

The target is the next close, which is usually near today’s close. This persistence explains why all models can achieve very high R² while barely improving RMSE over the naive forecast. Trade returns depend on changes, execution and costs rather than the chart’s upward trend alone.

Forecasting models

Every model predicts the next close. Every model is judged against one baseline: tomorrow equals today.

How each model was trained and tested

The same steps for every model, so the comparison is fair.

On 53.13% of test days the price rose, so a model that always says "up" scores 53.13%. LSTM and the Transformer match that exactly. The original naive-only run used a slightly different split (566 test sessions) and scored RMSE 7.3675, MAE 5.2050, MAPE 1.9653% and R² 0.9936.

How much better than copying today's close?

Change in test RMSE against the baseline. Right of zero is better.

The incremental forecasting gain is small.

The FT-Transformer improves test RMSE by about 0.164%; LSTM by 0.132%; stacking is about 1.079% worse than persistence. This chart measures price-forecast error reduction, not return or a proven trading edge.

Why the numbers look so alike. A forecast of "same as today" is already off by only about 2% a day, because prices move slowly relative to their level. To beat it, a model must predict the day-to-day change, and these models found almost nothing there. R² and MAPE barely move, and the differences between the top models (a few cents of RMSE) are far smaller than the day-to-day noise.

Model by model

Naive baseline

Forecast of tomorrow's close is today's close. Tested on its own, it predicts no moves at all, so a trading rule that waits for a 1% predicted gain never trades. Over the same test window, buy-and-hold returned +168.62% (1,000,000 → 2,686,246).

ARIMA

24 fits: three input sets (all 36 features, 8 curated features, close only) across eight (p,1,q) orders. Six fits did not converge, all with the full feature set, whose inputs are highly correlated (condition number 1,538 against 2.7 for the curated set). The simplest model won, a random walk (0,1,0), identical to the baseline.

Its residuals still show autocorrelation (Ljung–Box p < 10⁻⁶), and its 95% intervals contained the actual price only 40.8% of the time. The intervals are too narrow, probably because the model was fitted when prices, and dollar moves, were much smaller.

SARIMA

48 fits: three input sets, four non-seasonal orders and four seasonal choices, with a 5-session season (one trading week). The winner is close-only, (0,1,0)(0,1,1)₅. Its validation gain over the baseline is 0.031%, and 0.029% on test. A feature selector (elastic net) kept only three inputs for the exogenous version: daily log return, open-to-close change and the 3-day lagged return.

Simply repeating the price from 5 sessions ago is far worse (RMSE 5.00 on validation, 13.37 on test), so the weekly pattern is weak. Interval coverage was 40.4%.

XGBoost

Predicts the next dollar change, then adds it to today's close. 12 candidates (full, curated and close-history features across four parameter sets). The winner used 8 curated features, depth 2, learning rate 0.03 and just one boosting round, so it makes a very small correction and calls 94% of validation days "up".

Test direction accuracy is 53.31%, a hair above the always-up 53.13%.

LSTM

Close-only sequences of 20 days, 64 hidden units, one layer (17,217 parameters), trained with AdamW, batch 64 and learning rate 0.001. 24 setups were screened; the top two were repeated on three seeds (42, 123, 2026), giving mean validation RMSE 2.2311 ± 0.0055. The final model was refitted on train plus validation for 3 epochs. It learns a correction added to the last known close.

FT-Transformer

Treats each of 35 features (year excluded) as a token and lets them attend to each other: embedding 32, four heads, two layers, dropout 0.1, with volume log-transformed. Early stopping chose epoch 1 of up to 80. It is a feature model, not an attention model over a long price history.

Stacking

The stack learns how to combine models from out-of-sample forecasts built over five expanding time folds. Three stacks were compared; the chosen one was LSTM + Transformer + XGBoost with a Ridge meta-model (alpha 10). It did worse than every single model on test (RMSE 7.4811, 1.08% worse than baseline). A plain average of the selected pool of models did better (RMSE 7.3884, +0.17%, 53.85% direction), which suggests the meta-model fitted noise.

The stacked model is excluded from all three trading systems.

MODEL LAB / TRAINING BEFORE TRADING

How models are trained—and where they enter the trades.

The trading notebooks restore saved artifacts; they do not retrain six models inside every weekly or monthly simulation. Model fitting, strategy selection and trade execution are three separate stages.

TRAIN · 2,604 origins
18 Nov 2011 – 25 Mar 2022
Fit candidates and preprocessing
VALIDATE · 558 origins
28 Mar 2022 – 14 Jun 2024
Choose models and settings
TEST · 559 origins
17 Jun 2024 – 09 Sep 2026
Predict next-session closes

Target dates are one observation later: train ends 28-Mar-2022, validation ends 17-Jun-2024 and test ends 10-Sep-2026. These are chronological splits of 3,721 aligned samples; the raw history contains 3,771 rows.

01 · Prepare without future inputs

Build origin-date features and next-close targets. Fit scalers on the fitting partition; transform later rows with those scalers. LSTM windows create an additional warm-up. Its internal stopping split uses 2,163 fitting / 382 stopping windows.

02 · Select, refit, freeze

Validation determines configurations or epoch counts. Refit the selected model on train + validation before producing test forecasts. ARIMA / SARIMA subsequently update state with observed prices; this is distinct from re-estimating model parameters.

03 · Convert forecasts into decisions

Align each forecast with its origin and target. Restore the target contract: price directly for statistical models; origin-close plus learned correction for neural models / XGBoost. Newer notebooks compare reconstructed forecasts to saved references before searching trading rules.

ARIMA · Random-walk price baseline

Order (0,1,0); close-only; no exogenous inputs. Compare order / feature candidates by validation RMSE, MAE and complexity. Refit train + validation; forecast one step, then extend state with the observed close.

Saved test RMSE: 7.40127 price units.

All five forecasts enter annual consensus. A neutral price forecast contributes no directional edge.

SARIMA · Weekly seasonal price structure

Selected (0,1,0) × (0,1,1,5), close-only. Exogenous candidates were tested, but the winning model uses none. Choose by validation accuracy; refit train + validation, then extend state after each observation.

Saved test RMSE: 7.39913 price units.

One of the five forecast streams in the corrected newer engines and legacy annual engine.

LSTM · Learn a correction to the known close

Close-only sequence, lookback 20, hidden size 64, one recurrent layer. Screen 24 configurations; top two are checked on seeds 42 / 123 / 2026. AdamW, MSE, batch 64, learning rate 0.001; early stopping. Fresh train + validation refit: 3 epochs, seed 42. Restore scalers and add origin-close anchor at inference.

Saved test RMSE: 7.39152 price units.

Requires the inclusive origin window. A good price fit does not imply that each predicted change is tradable.

FT-Transformer · Attend across tabular feature tokens

35 features (Year excluded); log1p Volume and standard scaling. Embedding 32, four heads, two layers, feed-forward 64, dropout 0.1. AdamW 0.001, batch 32; up to 80 epochs, patience 10. Best epoch 1; fresh train + validation refit for one epoch. Add the predicted correction to origin Close.

Saved test RMSE: 7.38916 price units.

This is a feature-token model, not an attention model over a long price sequence.

XGBoost · Predict the next dollar change

Target = next Close − origin Close. Selected eight curated return / range / volatility / volume features. Depth 2, learning rate 0.03, one boosting round; squared-error objective. Validation selects the candidate and round count; refit train + validation with fixed settings. No scaling or Volume log transform.

Saved test RMSE: 7.40069 price units.

Convert its output back to price by adding origin Close. The yearly notebook incorrectly uses the raw change as a price.

Stacking · Learn from base-model out-of-fold forecasts

Five expanding chronological folds create base predictions for meta-training. Selected stack: LSTM + FT-Transformer + XGBoost with Ridge alpha 10. Meta-target is next-close change. Compare stacks on validation RMSE / MAE, then refit bases and selected stack for test.

Saved test RMSE: 7.48115 price units.

Saved meta-model is loaded but excluded from all three trading decision engines. It must not be credited for their profit.

How to read the forecast chart

Right of zero is lower error than simply predicting the current close; left is worse. FT-Transformer improves RMSE by only 0.164%, LSTM by 0.132%; stacking is about 1.08% worse. The axis is percentage improvement in error, not a trading return.

Why this does not explain profit by itself

Accurate price levels can still give poor direction or signals smaller than costs. LSTM and Transformer direction scores equal the 53.13% always-up baseline in these saved tests. Profit depends on rule selection, timing, sizing and exits, not just the model RMSE.
Input / role Long horizon Short horizon Advanced
ARIMA / SARIMA / LSTM / Transformer / XGBoost All five feed normalized consensus All five available to model-rule candidates All five combine into ONE model specialist
Selected technical rules Regime gates and position management Winning fit = 5-session price breakout Four technical specialists plus model specialist
Stacking Loaded; excluded Loaded; excluded Loaded; excluded
Direct explanation of saved monthly profit Not a monthly comparison Three technical breakout trades Four short trades; range-reversion attribution

In the advanced system, the model specialist uses inverse prior-40-session absolute forecast errors to weight models. Specialist routing then uses lagged reward estimates and profile priorities. “Range reversion” trade attribution identifies the strongest entry component; it does not prove other components had no influence.

Long-horizon system: consensus and pyramiding

Five models vote on direction, a trend filter decides when buying is allowed, and winning positions are added to in steps. It only buys; it never shorts.

From forecasts to orders

Top row builds the signal. Bottom row, read right to left, turns it into trades.

How a signal is built

  • Each model's forecast becomes an expected return: (forecast − close) ÷ close.
  • Each return is scaled by the median and MAD of the previous 63 sessions, then clipped to ±5.
  • A model's weight is its recent directional hit rate, kept between 0.40 and 0.70.
  • Consensus is the weighted score. Agreement is the larger share of models pointing one way.
  • A regime score blends EMA structure, trend strength (ADX), RSI, MACD, 5 and 20-day momentum, 20-day breakouts, volume and a penalty for a jump in volatility.

When it buys and how much

  • All must hold: EMA50 above EMA200, EMA10 above EMA20, close above EMA20, agreement at least 0.40, smoothed regime above −0.20, and consensus above its adaptive threshold.
  • Threshold: the larger of 0.18 and the 40th percentile of the previous 80 signals.
  • First buy uses 100% of cash if consensus is above 1.6× the threshold, 70% above 1.2×, otherwise 40%.
  • At +4% from the first buy it adds 30% of the remaining cash. At +8% it adds all of it, as long as consensus stays above the threshold.

How it exits

  • Orders fill at the next open with 10 bps combined commission and slippage per side.
  • First check, in this order: a hard stop at 5% below the first buy; a trailing stop 3 ATR below the highest close (widening to 4, 5 and 6 ATR once the trade is up 10%, 20% and 30%); at +8% a floor of +2% profit; at +15% a floor of +8%.
  • Then: after 90 observations if consensus is negative, or if EMA10 drops below EMA20 while consensus is negative.
  • After a sale it waits one observation if the uptrend is intact, otherwise three.
  • There is no forced sale at the end. The last position is valued at the final close.

Results

Account value against buy-and-hold

7 April 2025 to 9 September 2026. Both start at 100,000 on 7 April 2025. The strategy was in cash until its first buy on 27 May.

Positive profit is not benchmark outperformance.

The saved strategy grows more slowly than the equity-sheet buy-and-hold series. That benchmark starts on 7 April 2025; the workbook’s headline 137.77% buy-and-hold figure uses a different start. The annual ledger also marks next-open holdings against the prior close, so daily risk statistics retain a timing limitation.

Price with every buy and sell

Three buys on the fourth trade (30 Dec 2025, 6 Jan and 21 Jan 2026) are the pyramid. The last buy on 10 September 2026 is the open position.

Markers are executions, not signals.

Orders execute at the following open after a close-based decision. An additional buy can be a pyramid leg in an existing position rather than a new independent trade. Fifteen order events reconcile to six completed positions plus the final open holding.

Profit on each closed position

Includes every pyramid buy in that position.

Position-level accounting includes every purchase leg.

The final workbook reconciles all pyramid entries before computing completed-position profit. Gross gains of 50,261.78 less gross losses of 7,904.98 produce 42,356.80 realized profit. Adding 271.63 of open-position profit gives the 42,628.43 headline.

Drop from the previous peak

Daily closing values, in percent.

Drawdown is a decline from a previous portfolio peak.

A value of −17.53% means that the saved daily portfolio valuation fell that far below its preceding high. It is not the total return or a per-trade stop. Prior-close marking after next-open fills limits the reliability of this legacy series.

It made money but trailed the stock. Holding from the first forecast date returned +137.77%, and holding from 7 April 2025 returned about +198%. The strategy spent a lot of time in cash during a strong uptrend. The risk numbers (CAGR, Sharpe, drawdown) are reported as produced; the daily equity series has a one-day timing offset after next-open fills, so they should be treated as approximate.

All 15 order events

Long-horizon: complete execution specification

The compact flow above explains the sequence. The operational diagram below includes decision branches and the return to the next observation; the accompanying rules describe the saved implementation.

Data and forecast-to-signal pipeline

  • The saved forecast frame has 559 sessions, from 18-Jun-2024 through 10-Sep-2026. The trading loop waits until index 200. Its equity export begins 07-Apr-2025.
  • ARIMA, SARIMA, XGBoost, LSTM and Transformer are active. Stacking is loaded but excluded from consensus because the meta-model alone is not a complete inference pipeline.
  • Each model output becomes (prediction − current Close) / current Close. Lagged 63-session median/MAD scaling produces a Z score clipped to ±5.
  • Lagged directional reliability, clipped to 0.40–0.70, weights valid scores. Agreement is the larger of positive and negative score fractions; it is not specifically bullish agreement.
  • Smoothed regime combines EMA structure, ADX-like strength, RSI, MACD, 5/20-session momentum, 20-session breakouts, volume and an ATR-expansion penalty.

Rules that actually enter and add

  • Entry: EMA50 > EMA200, EMA10 > EMA20, Close > EMA20, agreement ≥0.40, smoothed regime >−0.20, and consensus above its adaptive threshold.
  • Bull threshold: max(0.18, prior-80-signal 40th percentile). The non-bull branch uses max(0.35, 65th percentile), although the mandatory bullish trend gate prevents flat non-bull entries.
  • Initial cash allocation: 100% if consensus >1.6×threshold; 70% if >1.2×; otherwise 40%. Fractional shares are allowed.
  • At +4% from initial entry, add 30% of remaining cash; at +8%, add all remaining cash, while consensus stays above threshold. These are not fixed 40→70→100% portfolio tiers.

Exit hierarchy, execution and terminal holdings

  • Orders execute at the next open with 10 bps combined commission/slippage per side. This system is long-only.
  • Hard stop: initial entry ×0.95. The close-based high-water trail is 3 ATR, rising to 4/5/6 ATR at +10/+20/+30%. At +8%, lock a minimum +2%; at +15%, lock +8%.
  • Exit priority: hard stop → ATR/profit-lock trail → holding counter ≥90 with negative consensus → EMA10
  • Cooldown is set to 1 if bullish trend remains, otherwise 3, and decremented at the start of the next iteration. A value of 1 permits evaluation again on that next iteration.
  • The active v2 engine uses signal-strength allocation tiers, not the unused annual-volatility target or 25-day holding constant from the config cell.
  • There is no final forced sale. Final equity equals cash plus remaining shares marked at the final close; the last position therefore has unrealized profit.

A · Equity: growth and benchmark context

The strategy finishes at 142,628.43 in the headline account. This plot uses the workbook’s daily marks and its later-start benchmark. It is not the same period as the 137.77% headline buy-and-hold calculation. Daily marks have a next-open timing defect, so the path and risk statistics need qualification.

Short-horizon system: rule search with intraday brackets

Instead of trusting the models, this system searches 2,088 simple rules and trades one. Every trade lasts a single day, so it ends each day in cash.

How the two rules were chosen

The same trade engine runs both rules. Only the way the rule is picked differs.

The rule that looks best (historical fit)

  • Take the previous close and compare it with its 5-session average, in units of the 5-session standard deviation (a z-score).
  • Above +1.5: go long. Below −1.5: go short. Otherwise stay in cash.
  • Enter at the next open. Put a stop and a target each 0.5 × the prior 14-day ATR from the entry price.
  • If both appear in one daily candle, the stop is assumed to hit first. If neither hits, exit at the close.

The fairer comparison (earlier-selected)

  • A 10-session z-score mean reversion rule at ±1.5, with a 1.5 ATR stop and a 3 ATR target.
  • Picked using only the first 515 sessions: top 50 from the first 383, then the best on the next 132.
  • It scored +38.75% in development and +63.89% in validation, yet lost 1.37% in the final month.

What one trade looks like

Stop and target are set from the prior ATR when the trade opens, and all trades close by the end of the day.

Position size and costs

  • Size is equity ÷ (1 + entry cost) in fractional shares, so the entry cost is paid from the account with no leverage.
  • Commission plus slippage is 10 bps per side. Shorts pay a 3% a year borrow charge for the one day.
  • At most one trade per session, and nothing is held overnight.

How lucky is the winner?

Out of 2,088 rules, only 402 (19%) made money in the monthly window, and just 80 (3.8%) made money in all three windows. The typical rule lost 1.7% in the month. The rule we report is the best of a big pool, picked after seeing the answer.

Every rule: development return against final-month return

Each dot is one rule. The filled dot is the historical-fit winner; the ring is the earlier-selected rule. The winner lost heavily in development (−15.32%) and validation (−16.79%).

Search dispersion is evidence of instability.

Each point represents one of 2,088 configurations, not an independent experiment. Rules sharing signals and parameters are highly related. The fitted winner loses in development and validation, while the earlier-selected winner loses in the final month; the selected tail profit does not demonstrate generalization.

Cost sensitivity

Return in the 22-session window against cost per side

Each point is a full re-run at that cost with the rules unchanged.

Costs reduce the same rule’s result.

The curve reruns the selected rule under different nominal per-side costs. It is not a new optimization at each point. Short borrowing is separate. Profit surviving higher modeled costs does not remove the use of the evaluation window in historical-fit selection.

What if shorting were switched off?

Return of the short-horizon system if it takes long trades only. Dropping the short trades changes the monthly historical-fit result from +2.54% to +1.12%.

Trades

The monthly historical-fit account made three trades, all closing in profit. Two were long and one short.

Trades in every window and both selection methods
Window summary, all six runs

Short-horizon: complete execution specification

The compact flow above explains the sequence. The operational diagram below includes decision branches and the return to the next observation; the accompanying rules describe the saved implementation.

Search and parameter selection

  • 2,088 configurations combine momentum, reversal, z-score breakout/reversion, RSI, candle direction, model signals and contrarian model signals with ATR stop/target settings.
  • Long-only and long/short versions are tested. Signal duplicates are removed using the pre-evaluation region.
  • Earlier selection: first 383 sessions, at least 30 active development days, top 50 development returns; the next 132 observations select the winner. The final 44 observations do not select its parameters.
  • Historical selection maximizes monthly net return subject to positive results in all three tail windows, when feasible. This explicitly uses the evaluation outcomes.

Selected historical breakout rule

  • Calculate the origin Close’s deviation from its trailing 5-session mean, divided by the 5-session sample standard deviation. The origin session is included.
  • z >+1.5 → long; z <−1.5 → short; otherwise cash. Enter at the next observed session’s open.
  • Stop and target are each 0.5×preceding simple rolling ATR14 from entry.
  • At most one completed position per session. Stop wins when both barriers appear inside a daily candle. Otherwise use the touched barrier, or exit at that session’s close. No overnight positions.

Position size, costs and comparison rule

  • Fractional-share notional is equity /(1+entry-cost rate), so entry cost is funded without leverage.
  • Nominal commission/slippage is 10 bps per side on actual entry/exit notional. Short borrow approximation is 3%/252 of entry notional for one day.
  • Earlier-selected rule: 10-session z-score mean reversion at ±1.5, with 1.5 ATR stop and 3 ATR target. The execution engine is otherwise identical.
  • The historical winner lost 15.32% in development and 16.79% in validation. Its profitable final windows contain only 1, 3 and 5 trades. These outcomes do not demonstrate stable profitability.

Advanced system: specialists, a router and a position lifecycle

Five specialists each score the market, a router trusts the ones that worked recently, and one account takes the net direction. It sizes by risk, takes partial profits and cuts risk when it is losing.

From five opinions to one trade

Top row builds the score. Bottom row, read right to left, handles size, fills, stops, costs and account limits.

The five specialists

SpecialistSignal
Trend pullbackEMA10 against EMA30 sets direction and price must stay on that side of EMA30. A fast RSI(3) below 55 allows long pullbacks; above 45 allows shorts.
Range reversion20-session z-score of the close: below −1 goes long, above +1 goes short. Full weight when ADX is under 30, 35% otherwise.
Price breakout5-session z-score of the close: above +1 goes long, below −1 goes short.
Compression breakoutActive when ATR is below its 40-session average today or yesterday; otherwise a half-strength 10-session channel breakout.
Model consensusModel expected returns weighted by the inverse of their absolute errors over the previous 40 sessions; scaled by daily volatility with tanh.

Routing and the winning profile

  • Each specialist gets a proxy reward: its score × the next open-to-close return, minus a small cost on |score|, delayed one day.
  • Its weight multiplier is exp(clip(3 × mean ÷ (std + 0.002), −1.5, +1.5)) over the previous 40 sessions, then combined with fixed profile priorities.
  • Seven profiles and 756 configurations were searched (7 profiles × 3 entry levels × 3 stops × 3 hold limits × 2 reward targets × 2 risk budgets).
  • Winner (historical fit): Mean reversion profile, entry at |score| ≥ 0.15, stop 0.6 ATR, hold up to 3 sessions, target 1.5R, 2% risk per trade.
  • Earlier-selected: Trend and pullback profile, entry 0.30, stop 1.0 ATR, hold up to 7 sessions, target 3R.

Sizing, gates and fills

  • No new trade if ATR is 8% or more of the previous close, the open gaps by 2.5 ATR or more, or the account is in a cool-down or halt.
  • Shares = the smallest of: risk budget ÷ stop distance, an exposure cap (40% volatility target) with a confidence cap, and 0.5% of prior volume.
  • Half of the shares exit at +1R. The rest exit at the final target, trailing stop, signal reversal or time limit.
  • A gap through a stop fills at the open. Stops are checked before targets.
  • Costs: 5 bps commission (minimum 1 unit), 5 bps slippage plus 20 × √(shares ÷ prior volume) bps, and 3% a year borrow on shorts.
  • A 5% drawdown halves new risk. A 12% drawdown halts new entries and exits what remains.

Where the monthly profit came from

All four winning monthly trades were short trades led by the range-reversion specialist. "Led by" means it had the largest share of the entry score; it does not prove the other specialists played no part.

The historical-fit profile lost 12.55% in development and 2.78% in validation. The earlier-selected Trend and pullback profile gained 5.27% and 3.23% there, but lost 7.05% in the final month. Neither result shows an edge that would carry forward.

Return against cost per side, 22 sessions

At 5 bps the historical-fit account earns 8.47%; at 40 bps it still earns 5.65%.

The cost test and the selection test answer different questions.

The fitted advanced month falls from approximately 8.47% at 5 bps to 5.65% at 40 bps, while the earlier-selected month remains negative. This indicates modeled cost tolerance in the fitted month, alongside weak evidence of performance beyond the selected period.

Trades in every window and both selection methods
Window summary, all six runs

Advanced: complete execution specification

The compact flow above explains the sequence. The operational diagram below includes decision branches and the return to the next observation; the accompanying rules describe the saved implementation.

Routing and the winning profile

  • Proxy reward = specialist score × target open-to-close return −0.002×|score|. Shift one observation before taking the trailing 40-session mean and standard deviation. This is a routing heuristic, not event-engine P&L.
  • Adaptive multiplier = exp(clip(3×mean /(std+0.002), −1.5, +1.5)). Multiply by base profile priorities, normalize, then sum weighted specialist scores.
  • Seven profiles are searched. Only the profile named Regime rotation additionally changes weights with ADX>25. Regime labels do not switch all profiles.
  • Historical winner: Mean reversion profile with base weights [0.5, 3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.5] in the order above. Entry |score|≥0.15; stop 0.6 ATR; hold cap 3; final target 1.5R; risk budget 2%.
  • 756 configurations =7 profiles ×3 entry gates ×3 stop distances ×3 holding caps ×2 reward multiples ×2 risk budgets. Earlier selection screens at least 20 development trades and 5 validation trades, then takes the top 50 development returns and selects on the following 132-session validation return. The final 44 observations are excluded from that selection.

Risk-based whole-share sizing

  • Block entry during cooldown/halt, when ATR/prior Close ≥8%, or |opening gap| ≥2.5 ATR. This gap gate uses the entry open, not solely prior-close information.
  • Exposure cap = min(1, 0.40/max(annualized 20-session volatility, 0.05)). Confidence cap = min(1, 0.5+|score|).
  • Shares = floor(min(cash×risk×drawdown scaling /stop distance, cash×exposure×confidence /cost-buffered open, 0.005×preceding volume)).
  • Prior end-of-day drawdown >5% halves risk. Below −12%, halt new entries for the remainder of the run; any existing holding exits at a subsequent open. Gap losses can exceed those thresholds.

Fill hierarchy, partial profits and costs

  • For an existing position: gap-through stop fills at open; a favorable gap beyond final target uses the target price; risk-halt or strong opposite score otherwise exits at open. No same-bar re-entry after closing.
  • If the position survives the stop, half its whole shares exit at +1R. The balance exits at reward×R, time limit or window-end close. Stop takes precedence when both stop and target are touched.
  • After survival, the high/low-based 1.5 ATR trail tightens for the next session. After partial profit, protection is at least break-even. A new trail is not retroactively tested against that candle.
  • Commission: 5 bps of executed notional with a one-unit minimum. Slippage: 5 bps +20×sqrt(shares/prior volume) bps. Borrow: short opening notional ×0.03/252 per modeled session.
  • Loss cooldown: one session, or two after consecutive losses. The flag is calculated before exit-day borrow, so near-zero trades may be classified differently from their final net P&L.
  • Saved Hold_sessions increments in the intraday branch; an opening-gap exit can undercount inclusive holding observations. Entry and exit dates are authoritative.

05 / FORECAST CONTRACT & COSTS

Same saved artifacts. Different forecast handling.

Model Artifact Corrected short / advanced inference Long-horizon implementation difference
ARIMA / SARIMA selected_model.pkl Saved cutoff state → forecast target → observe target → extend state Legacy arrays use different current-row alignment.
XGBoost selected_model.ubj Predict dollar change; add origin Close to reconstruct target price Raw dollar change is treated as a price.
LSTM selected_model.pt and saved x/y scalers Inclusive origin lookback; origin-close anchor; inverse target scaling Legacy window ends before its displayed row.
Transformer selected_model.pt and saved x/y scalers Origin features/Close anchor; log1p Volume when metadata requires Legacy inference omits saved Volume log transform.
Stacking selected_meta.joblib Loaded but not used for decisions; full base reconstruction absent Also excluded from old consensus.

Neural architectures are reconstructed from checkpoint metadata and local model_definition.py; state dictionaries are loaded strictly. Fresh forecasts come from saved models. In the newer notebooks, test_predictions.csv files are used to audit date alignment and output parity, not as trading inputs. The trading notebooks do not retrain models.

Why the headline profits are not one comparable ranking

System Period Position treatment Decision source Interpretation
Long horizon Multi-month saved run; equity starts 07-Apr-2025 Long only; final holding stays open Five-model normalized consensus Saved outcome with legacy timing/inference defects
Short horizon Independent final 5 /22 /44 sessions Long / short; flat each day One selected price rule; model rules also searched Historical fit plus earlier-selected comparator
Advanced Independent final 5 /22 /44 sessions Long / short; multi-session; partial exits Adaptive specialists including model score Historical fit plus earlier-selected comparator

Putting the three side by side

The headline profits answer different questions, so they should not be ranked against each other.

SystemPeriodPositionsWhat drives the decision
Long horizonAbout 17 months, from 7 April 2025Long only; the last position is still openFive-model consensus plus trend and regime filters
Short horizonFinal 5, 22 and 44 sessions, each its own accountLong and short; flat every nightOne price rule; model-based rules were searched but did not win
AdvancedFinal 5, 22 and 44 sessions, each its own accountLong and short; held up to several sessions, partial exitsRouter over five specialists, one of which uses the models

Do the models earn the profit?

Only in the long-horizon system, where all five forecasts feed the consensus. In the short-horizon system the winning rule is a price breakout. In the advanced system the model specialist is one of five, and the monthly profits trace to range reversion. The stacked model is not used anywhere.

What would make the evidence stronger

  • Test on a later period nobody has looked at yet.
  • Re-pick the rules on a rolling basis, so every score is out of sample.
  • Report results over many more trades than 3 or 4.
  • Check fills against intraday data, not daily candles.

What the combined evidence supports

Observed result

The long-horizon account is profitable in absolute terms. The short fitted rule has the strongest 44-session result of the two newer systems, while the advanced fitted rule has the strongest 22-session result. This ranking changes by window and must be stated with its period and selection method.

The advanced monthly profit is concentrated in four range-reversion-attributed short trades. That attribution identifies the largest score contribution at entry; it does not measure how much profit each forecasting model caused.

Evidence needed next

Freeze the rule and its preprocessing before evaluating a new chronological period. Compare against the same dates, execution prices, capital and cost assumptions; report realized and open profit separately. Use repeated walk-forward windows to measure variability rather than reporting only the best tail.

Ablations can test the model contribution: rerun the same engine with price-only specialists, the model specialist alone, and the combined score. Any improvement should be evaluated after costs on observations not used to choose that variant.

Reading the metrics correctly

MetricMeaning in this reportInterpretation
Net profitFinal equity minus 100,000Includes modeled charges; annual final equity includes an open mark.
ReturnNet profit / 100,000 × 100Window return, not annualized; +8.08% is the reported month only.
DrawdownEquity / running peak − 1Daily marks omit within-session risk.
Win rateWinning completed positions / completed positions100% across three or four trades provides little precision about a future win rate.
Profit factorGross completed-position gains / absolute losses6.3582 for the corrected annual ledger; a no-loss sample cannot establish a stable factor.
Forecast skill1 − model RMSE / naive RMSEA small positive forecast gain is not the same as a profitable executable signal.

Checks and limits

What reconciles, and what a reader should keep in mind.

What reconciles

PassLong-horizon profit42,356.80 realized + 271.63 unrealized = 42,628.43. All six closed positions include every pyramid buy. An earlier tally missed some pyramid legs and gave a profit factor of 5.36; the corrected value is 6.36.
PassShort-horizon accountsFor all six runs, the sum of trade profits equals final equity minus 100,000.
PassAdvanced accountsCompleted-trade profits match each of the six summaries within rounding.
PassForecast reconstructionFor the two newer systems, forecasts rebuilt from the saved models match the stored forecasts on all 559 rows for all five models, with zero error.

What to keep in mind

BiasRules fitted to the scored daysThe short-horizon and advanced "historical fit" rules were chosen using the final 5, 22 and 44 sessions. Their profits are in-sample. The earlier-selected rules are shown next to them for that reason, though the data has been looked at before.
SampleVery few tradesThe monthly historical-fit results rest on 3 or 4 trades, and drawdown uses daily closes, so it hides losses inside the day.
FillsDaily candles onlyDaily highs and lows cannot show which came first, queue position or short availability. Stop-first is the cautious assumption; costs and borrow are assumptions too.
TimingLong-horizon equity seriesAfter a next-open fill, the equity export logs shares against the previous day's close. It showed shares on 9 September for a buy dated 10 September. That can distort daily returns, drawdown and Sharpe.
ForecastsOlder forecast routine in the long-horizon runIt treated XGBoost's raw dollar change as a price, skipped the Transformer's volume log-transform, and used shifted rows for ARIMA and SARIMA. The newer systems fixed these. The long-horizon results were kept as run rather than recomputed.
BenchmarksDifferent start datesThe +137.77% buy-and-hold figure starts at the first forecast date; the chart benchmark starts on 7 April 2025. The long-horizon name suggests a year, but the forecast frame covers 559 sessions and trading begins at observation 200.
CurrencyUnitsThe long-horizon output printed ₹ but prices and targets are in USD, with no conversion. All amounts here are plain simulation units.
ScopeNot investment adviceThese are backtests of specific rules on one stock. They do not show that any rule is profitable in the future.
06 / RECONCILIATION & SOURCES

What reconciles, and what needs qualification.

Check / issue Finding
PASS · yearly profit 42,356.80 realized +271.63 unrealized =42,628.43 total. Six reconstructed completed positions include every pyramid purchase.
PASS · short horizon Net trade P&L equals final equity minus 100,000 for all six saved runs.
PASS · advanced Completed-trade net P&L matches each of the six summary outcomes within rounding.
SOURCE CORRECTION · profit factor Use final workbook: gross profit 50,261.78; average completed trade 7,059.47; profit factor 6.3582. Older CSV gives 42,344.61 /5,739.94 /5.3567 because pyramid legs are not fully included in trade-level accounting.
PERIOD · yearly name 559 forecast sessions cover Jun-2024 to Sep-2026. Trading begins at index 200. Equity export: 07-Apr-2025 to 09-Sep-2026; final headline mark: 10-Sep-2026. This is not one calendar year.
TIMING · yearly equity Next-open fills update shares/cash before the loop logs equity against the previous signal-day close. The export shows shares on 09-Sep for the BUY dated 10-Sep. This can distort daily returns, drawdown, Sharpe and annualized statistics. They remain reported values, not independently validated metrics.
BENCHMARK · different origins Yearly headline buy-and-hold 137.77% uses the full forecast-frame start. The Equity Curve sheet rebases at later 07-Apr-2025. The chart uses that sheet and explicitly labels it; the reported headline benchmark is preserved separately.
FORECAST · legacy mismatch Old XGBoost output near 0.0013 is a dollar change treated as a price, producing about −99.999% implied return in its diagnostics. Model date alignment differs; Transformer Volume preprocessing also differs from training. Saved results were not silently repaired or rerun.
CURRENCY · source conflict Yearly workbook prints ₹, but model metadata specifies USD targets and there is no FX conversion. Numerical values are retained as neutral simulation units.
SELECTION · optimized tails Short and advanced historical-fit rules use the final windows to select parameters. Their earlier losses and negative earlier-selected monthly results are shown beside the profits.
EXECUTION · daily candles OHLC cannot identify precise intraday barrier order, queue position, short inventory or fill quality. Stop-first handling is conservative, but costs and borrow remain assumptions. Advanced favorable gap targets use target price rather than the better open.
RISK · limited samples Monthly historical-fit results use only three or four trades. End-of-day drawdown excludes intraday losses. Annual open holdings and daily-flat newer accounts use different terminal conventions.
SCOPE · source preservation This report consolidates and qualifies saved evidence. It does not change source workbooks, notebooks, models, rules or results, and does not optimize new parameters.

Source map

  • Yearly headline / corrected trades: TSMC_Trading_Pipeline_Strategy_Results_Final.xlsx → Performance, Trade Analysis, Trade Log, Equity Curve and Audit Notes.

  • Advanced results: advanced_report/TSMC_Advanced_Report.xlsx → Summary, Trades, Daily accounts, Executions, Selected rules, Research, Costs and forecast audit.
  • Rules, forecasting and diagrams: active code in TSMC_Trading_Simulation_Professional_v3.ipynb, TSMC_Short_Horizon_Weekly_Monthly_2Months.ipynb and TSMC_Advanced_Multi_Strategy.ipynb. Superseded descriptive markdown is not treated as the execution specification.
  • Source precedence: final user workbook for corrected annual trade metrics; per-run ledgers for outcomes; active notebook code for implementation. Any discrepancy is documented above.
